title: Chapter 30 — The Pipe
paragraphs: When Stubb had gone, Ahab stood for a while leaning over the bulwarks. Then, as had become his habit lately, he called a sailor on watch and sent him below for his ivory stool and his pipe. Lighting the pipe at the compass lamp and planting the stool on the windward side of the deck, he sat and smoked.

In old Norse times, the thrones of the sea-loving Danish kings were built, according to tradition, from the tusks of the narwhal. How could anyone look at Ahab then, seated on that tripod of bones, without thinking of the royalty it symbolized? For Ahab was a king of the planks, a lord of the sea, and a great ruler of Leviathans.

Some moments passed while thick smoke came from his mouth in quick, constant puffs that blew back into his face. "What's this?" he said at last, pulling the pipe from his mouth. "This smoking no longer soothes me. Oh, my pipe! Things must be going badly for me if your charm is gone! I've been toiling here without realizing it, not taking pleasure — yes, and foolishly smoking to windward all the while, with such nervous, anxious puffs, as if, like the dying whale, my final gasps were the strongest and most troubled. What business do I have with this pipe? This thing is meant for serenity, for sending up mild white vapors among mild white hairs — not among torn iron-gray locks like mine. I'll smoke no more —"

He tossed the still-lit pipe into the sea. The fire hissed in the waves. At the same instant, the ship shot past the bubble the sinking pipe made. With his hat pulled low, Ahab lurched across the planks.
